advances: Actual globally critical caps can pair after restriction to each integer fiber while their ambient planes are all distinct.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The only integer bases in \([0,1]\) are \(0\) and \(1\), both with fiber \(B\). Thus the total mass is \(2V\). At either center every containing halfspace captures at least half of its own ball. Conversely, at any point \((j,y)\) in the mixed set, use a unit vector \(u\) with \(u\cdot y\ge0\) and a cap through that point whose restriction at \(j\) is \(u\cdot x\ge u\cdot y\). A base tilt with magnitude greater than \(1\), directed to increase the threshold at the other base, makes the other trace empty. The own cap has volume at most \(V/2\) by symmetry, so no point exceeds that depth.

For each displayed cap, the other base has threshold \(L>1\), and its own base has threshold zero. Hence the cap has mass \(V/2\), is critical at the stated center, and captures a central hemisphere. The opposite continuous normals at each base sum to zero. The other trace stays empty for small shifts in the threshold. The own cap mass has two-sided derivative equal to minus the central \((d-1)\)-dimensional section volume, since its slice areas vary continuously there. These derivatives agree for all four caps. Thus the two caps at each mark can receive the equal within-circuit weights, and taking equal circuit weights gives \(1/4\) per cap. On each ball boundary off the central cutting plane exactly one of the two own caps captures the point and both foreign caps are empty, proving the score statement.

In ambient coordinates the four boundary equations are \(x_1=Lz\), \(x_1=-Lz\), \(x_1=L-Lz\), and \(x_1=Lz-L\). Lines of different slope in the \((z,x_1)\)-plane are distinct, and the two with each common slope have intercept difference \(L>0\). Their ambient extensions are therefore all distinct. Restriction to a fixed integer base collapses only the corresponding pair to one properly cutting plane.

source_sections.locator: §5, first example, the actual two-ball critical caps

statement: Let \(d\ge2\), let \(B\subset\mathbb R^d\) be the unit Euclidean ball of volume \(V\), and let \(C=[0,1]\times B\). Give the actual integer fibers of \(C\) their \(d\)-volume. Both \((0,0)\) and \((1,0)\) attain the global maximum raw halfspace depth \(V/2\), with normalized value \(1/4\). For any \(L>1\), the two closed halfspaces with margins \(\pm x_1-Lz\) at base \(0\) and those with margins \(\pm x_1+L(z-1)\) at base \(1\) form positive critical pairs at these marks. Each cap has mass \(V/2\) and the same positive two-sided threshold slope in magnitude. With weight \(1/4\) on each of the four caps, the restricted score on each ball boundary away from the cuts is \(1/4\) and the two proper restrictions there have the same plane with opposite orientations. The four ambient boundary planes are pairwise distinct.
title: Actual critical caps can pair in the fibers with distinct ambient planes
